cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and the light you steer by is still where it was.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: For this week, carry your own share of the pressure and nobody else's. When you would normally reach across and take up someone else's part, keep your hands where they are and leave theirs alone. No clock — you will know when it comes up.
cells.core:
There is a light you steer by, and you are still moving toward it. Not because it is easy, but because you have carried a direction through real pressure, and you can watch that becoming something you rely on. A person doing this well arrives somewhere and notices that they arrived. That noticing is what all the persistence was for.

What is not fair is the weight. A chunk of your load is other people's — taken up quietly, mostly unasked, at your own expense — and that is the part that is bending. Carry your own share, all of it, and leave the rest where it lies for a while. The point is not to stop caring. It is to find how much of the pressure you have been calling yours actually is.
cells.sheetLine: You are still following your light. Check what you are carrying that is not yours.
cells.verb: keep going after everything that's happened

cells.tense: You are projecting forward into a finish that has not arrived yet, bracing for outcomes you cannot write in.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Take something you are sure about — how this ends, what someone will do, what it all means — and sit with both sides of it for a few days before you speak. Say it after that, or do not. Sitting with it is the act.
cells.core:
You have a light you are steering by, and you have gotten ahead of it. The picture in your head is so detailed it feels real — the arrival, the reckoning, the moment it is finally settled — and you live inside that picture while the actual work moves at its own pace. Your certainty has outrun the evidence you actually have.

Doubting yourself is not the correction. The pause is. Stay with both sides for a few days before you say anything — what you hold, and what you do not yet. That pause keeps what you see accurate instead of imposed. It is also the way you let a right answer arrive without forcing it into place before its time.
cells.sheetLine: You are certain before the evidence has caught up. Stay with it before you speak.
cells.verb: keep going after everything that's happened

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that was already behind you, and the light you steer by has gone quiet.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Look after something that is still growing — a patch of work, a plant, a skill — on a regular rhythm, without measuring whether it is working. Leave the big light alone for now.
cells.core:
You steer by a light, or you did. Lately it has gone quiet, and your attention sits on upkeep rather than movement. The reach toward the thing feels larger than what you have on hand, so the reach stops, and the light stays dark, and the days fill with taking care of a place you are no longer in.

Do not try to relight the light. Tend something actual that is still growing — small, real, close by — with a steady hand, on a regular rhythm, without checking whether it is doing anything. That care rebuilds the road. You do not need the light to be burning in order to look after a living thing while it grows.
cells.sheetLine: The light is quiet. Tend what is still growing near you instead.
cells.verb: keep going after everything that's happened

cells.tense: The pen is in your hand in a room you are already writing, though you would say the words are someone else's.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: When you push through something hard this week, take a breath and register that you are the one doing it, on your own reserves, with no help. No ceremony. Then keep moving.
cells.core:
The light is being steered from somewhere you would describe as just how things are. The persistence you carry — going on when the pressure is real — gets filed under personality, or culture, or how the family worked, or how anybody would do it. You have a name for the version of this that other people have, and none for the one you are running.

The fix is small and awkward: notice who is doing it, while it is happening. Next time you push through material pressure, before you brush it off as nothing special, stop for a breath and register that it is you, on your own reserves. The strength you are using is yours, and it keeps holding because you keep showing up.
cells.sheetLine: It gets filed as just how things are. It is yours, and it is holding.
cells.verb: keep going after everything that's happened
